title: Two-sample t statistic
context: Compare group A and B means.
task: Set result to the t-statistic of an independent two-sample t-test (equal variance) comparing group B vs group A values, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value']
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value']
result = round(float(stats.ttest_ind(B, A).statistic), 3)

title: Two-sample p-value
task: Set result to the two-sided p-value of the independent t-test (equal variance) between groups B and A, rounded to 4 decimals.
answer:
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value']
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value']
result = round(float(stats.ttest_ind(B, A).pvalue), 4)

title: Welch's t-test p-value
task: Set result to the two-sided p-value of Welch's t-test (equal_var=False) between groups B and A, rounded to 4 decimals.
answer:
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value']
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value']
result = round(float(stats.ttest_ind(B, A, equal_var=False).pvalue), 4)

title: Reject at 0.05?
task: Set result to 'Reject H0' if the independent t-test (B vs A, equal var) p-value < 0.05, else 'Fail to reject'.
answer:
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value']
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value']
p = stats.ttest_ind(B, A).pvalue
result = 'Reject H0' if p < 0.05 else 'Fail to reject'

title: One-sample t-test
context: Is the sample mean different from 168?
task: Set result to the two-sided p-value of a one-sample t-test of sample x against a population mean of 168, rounded to 4 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.ttest_1samp(sample['x'], 168).pvalue), 4)

title: Paired t statistic
context: before vs after on the same subjects.
task: Set result to the t-statistic of a paired t-test of after vs before, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.ttest_rel(paired['after'], paired['before']).statistic), 3)

title: Paired t-test p-value
task: Set result to the two-sided p-value of the paired t-test (after vs before), rounded to 4 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.ttest_rel(paired['after'], paired['before']).pvalue), 4)

title: 95% CI lower bound
context: Confidence interval for the sample mean.
task: Set result to the lower bound of the 95% t-confidence interval for the mean of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer:
x = sample['x']
n = len(x)
ci = stats.t.interval(0.95, n - 1, loc=x.mean(), scale=x.std() / np.sqrt(n))
result = round(float(ci[0]), 2)

title: 95% CI upper bound
task: Set result to the upper bound of the 95% t-confidence interval for the mean of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer:
x = sample['x']
n = len(x)
ci = stats.t.interval(0.95, n - 1, loc=x.mean(), scale=x.std() / np.sqrt(n))
result = round(float(ci[1]), 2)

title: CI width
task: Set result to the width (upper − lower) of the 95% t-CI for the mean of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer:
x = sample['x']
n = len(x)
ci = stats.t.interval(0.95, n - 1, loc=x.mean(), scale=x.std() / np.sqrt(n))
result = round(float(ci[1] - ci[0]), 2)

title: 99% CI is wider
task: Set result to the width of the 99% t-CI for the mean of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer:
x = sample['x']
n = len(x)
ci = stats.t.interval(0.99, n - 1, loc=x.mean(), scale=x.std() / np.sqrt(n))
result = round(float(ci[1] - ci[0]), 2)

title: Pearson r and p
task: Set result to the Pearson correlation coefficient between hours and score, rounded to 3 decimals, using scipy.
answer: result = round(float(stats.pearsonr(regression['hours'], regression['score'])[0]), 3)

title: Correlation significance
task: Set result to the p-value of the Pearson correlation between hours and score, rounded to 6 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.pearsonr(regression['hours'], regression['score'])[1]), 6)

title: Spearman correlation
task: Set result to the Spearman correlation between hours and score, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.spearmanr(regression['hours'], regression['score']).correlation), 3)

title: Regression slope
task: Set result to the slope of the least-squares line of score on hours, rounded to 3 decimals, using scipy linregress.
answer: result = round(float(stats.linregress(regression['hours'], regression['score']).slope), 3)

title: Regression intercept
task: Set result to the intercept of the least-squares line of score on hours, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.linregress(regression['hours'], regression['score']).intercept), 3)

title: R-squared
task: Set result to the R-squared of the regression of score on hours (rvalue squared), rounded to 3 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.linregress(regression['hours'], regression['score']).rvalue ** 2), 3)

title: Predict a score
task: Set result to the predicted score for 6 study hours from the least-squares fit, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer:
r = stats.linregress(regression['hours'], regression['score'])
result = round(float(r.slope * 6 + r.intercept), 2)

title: Chi-square on the A/B test
task: Set result to the chi-square p-value from a 2×2 contingency table of [converted, not-converted] by variant, rounded to 4 decimals, using stats.chi2_contingency.
answer:
tbl = [[r['conversions'], r['visitors'] - r['conversions']] for _, r in experiment.iterrows()]
result = round(float(stats.chi2_contingency(tbl)[1]), 4)

title: Difference in conversion rates
task: Set result to the difference in conversion rate (treatment − control) as a percentage, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer:
e = experiment.set_index('variant')
rt = e.loc['treatment', 'conversions'] / e.loc['treatment', 'visitors']
rc = e.loc['control', 'conversions'] / e.loc['control', 'visitors']
result = round((rt - rc) * 100, 2)

title: Cohen's d
task: Set result to Cohen's d for B vs A = (mean B − mean A) / pooled std, rounded to 3 decimals. Use the pooled std with ddof=1.
answer:
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value']
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value']
nA, nB = len(A), len(B)
sp = np.sqrt(((nA - 1) * A.var() + (nB - 1) * B.var()) / (nA + nB - 2))
result = round(float((B.mean() - A.mean()) / sp), 3)

title: Shapiro-Wilk test
task: Set result to the p-value of the Shapiro-Wilk normality test on sample x, rounded to 4 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.shapiro(sample['x']).pvalue), 4)

title: Mann-Whitney U
task: Set result to the two-sided p-value of the Mann-Whitney U test comparing group B and A values, rounded to 4 decimals.
answer:
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value']
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value']
result = round(float(stats.mannwhitneyu(B, A).pvalue), 4)

title: Wilcoxon signed-rank
task: Set result to the two-sided p-value of the Wilcoxon signed-rank test on after vs before, rounded to 4 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.wilcoxon(paired['after'], paired['before']).pvalue), 4)

title: Fit a normal mean
task: Set result to the fitted mean (loc) of a normal distribution fit to sample x, rounded to 2 decimals, using stats.norm.fit.
answer: result = round(float(stats.norm.fit(sample['x'])[0]), 2)

title: Expected conversions
task: Set result to the expected number of conversions if 1000 visitors convert at the control rate, rounded to 1 decimal.
answer:
c = experiment[experiment['variant'] == 'control'].iloc[0]
result = round(1000 * c['conversions'] / c['visitors'], 1)

title: Normal-approx CI for a proportion
context: 95% CI half-width for the control rate.
task: Set result to the 95% margin of error for the control conversion proportion = 1.96 * sqrt(p(1-p)/n), rounded to 4 decimals.
answer:
c = experiment[experiment['variant'] == 'control'].iloc[0]
p = c['conversions'] / c['visitors']
result = round(1.96 * np.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / c['visitors']), 4)

title: Excess kurtosis
task: Set result to the excess kurtosis of sample x, rounded to 3 decimals, using scipy stats.
answer: result = round(float(stats.kurtosis(sample['x'])), 3)

title: Z statistic for a mean
task: Set result to the z-statistic testing whether sample x mean differs from 168, assuming population sigma = 10: z = (mean − 168) / (10/sqrt(n)), rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
x = sample['x']
result = round(float((x.mean() - 168) / (10 / np.sqrt(len(x)))), 3)

title: Largest residual
context: Where does the model miss most?
task: Set result to the maximum absolute residual (actual − predicted score) from the least-squares fit, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer:
r = stats.linregress(regression['hours'], regression['score'])
pred = r.slope * regression['hours'] + r.intercept
result = round(float((regression['score'] - pred).abs().max()), 2)

title: Covariance
task: Set result to the sample covariance (ddof=1) between hours and score, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(np.cov(regression['hours'], regression['score'])[0, 1]), 3)

title: Pooled standard deviation
task: Set result to the pooled standard deviation of groups A and B (ddof=1 pooled formula), rounded to 3 decimals.
hint: same pooled sd formula as Cohen's d.
answer:
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value']
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value']
nA, nB = len(A), len(B)
result = round(float(np.sqrt(((nA - 1) * A.var() + (nB - 1) * B.var()) / (nA + nB - 2))), 3)

title: Critical t-value
task: Set result to the two-tailed 95% critical t-value for the sample x degrees of freedom (n − 1), rounded to 4 decimals.
answer: result = round(float(stats.t.ppf(0.975, len(sample) - 1)), 4)
